problems.title: Two Sum
problems.statement:
You are given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`. Return the indices of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`.

Assume exactly one valid answer exists, and you may not use the same element twice. Return the indices in increasing order.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n (size of array) and target, space separated.
Second line: n space-separated integers.
problems.outputFormat: Two space-separated indices (0-indexed), smaller index first.
hints: A brute force checking every pair works but is O(n^2). Can you do better?
A hash map from value -> index lets you check 'have I seen target - nums[i] before?' in O(1).
Iterate once, and for each element check the complement before inserting the current element into the map.

problems.title: Maximum Subarray
problems.statement: Given an integer array `nums`, find the contiguous subarray (containing at least one number) which has the largest sum, and return that sum.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n.
Second line: n space-separated integers (may be negative).
problems.outputFormat: A single integer: the maximum subarray sum.
hints: Think about extending a running subarray sum vs starting fresh at the current element.
Kadane's algorithm: maintain `currentSum = max(nums[i], currentSum + nums[i])`.
Track a separate `best` variable updated every step, since the optimal subarray might end anywhere.

problems.title: Move Zeroes
problems.statement: Given an integer array `nums`, move all zeroes to the end of it while maintaining the relative order of the non-zero elements. Print the resulting array.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n.
Second line: n space-separated integers.
problems.outputFormat: n space-separated integers: the array after moving zeroes to the end.
hints: Use a 'write pointer' that tracks where the next non-zero element should go.
Do a single pass copying non-zero elements forward, then fill the rest with zeroes.
This can be done in-place in O(n) time and O(1) extra space.

problems.title: Product of Array Except Self
problems.statement: Given an integer array `nums`, return an array `answer` such that `answer[i]` is equal to the product of all the elements of `nums` except `nums[i]`. Do this without using division.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n.
Second line: n space-separated integers.
problems.outputFormat: n space-separated integers: the answer array.
constraints: The product of any prefix or suffix fits in a 64-bit integer.
hints: Compute prefix products (product of everything to the left) in one pass.
Compute suffix products (product of everything to the right) in a second pass.
answer[i] = prefix[i] * suffix[i]. You can do this with O(1) extra space beyond the output array.

problems.title: Trapping Rain Water
problems.statement: Given `n` non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n.
Second line: n space-separated non-negative integers (bar heights).
problems.outputFormat: A single integer: total units of trapped water.
hints: Water trapped above index i is min(maxLeft[i], maxRight[i]) - height[i], if positive.
Precompute maxLeft and maxRight arrays in O(n), or use a two-pointer approach for O(1) extra space.
With two pointers, move the side with the smaller current max inward, since that side's bound is already known.

problems.title: Reverse a Linked List
problems.statement: Given the values of a singly linked list, build the list and reverse it. Print the reversed list's values in order.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n (number of nodes).
Second line: n space-separated integers, the list values in order.
problems.outputFormat: n space-separated integers: the reversed list.
hints: Track three pointers: prev, current, and next, iterating through the list.
At each node, save next, point current->next to prev, then advance prev and current.
After the loop, prev is the new head.

problems.title: Detect Cycle in a Linked List
problems.statement: Given a linked list built from `n` values, and an integer `pos` indicating the index (0-indexed) that the tail connects back to (or -1 for no cycle), determine whether the list has a cycle.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n and pos, space separated.
Second line: n space-separated integers, the list values.
problems.outputFormat: Print "true" if a cycle exists, otherwise "false".

examples.explanation: The tail connects back to index 1, forming a cycle.

hints: Floyd's algorithm: a slow pointer moves 1 step, a fast pointer moves 2 steps.
If there's a cycle, the fast pointer will eventually catch up to the slow pointer.
If the fast pointer reaches nullptr, there is no cycle.

problems.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
problems.statement: You are given two linked lists, each sorted in non-decreasing order. Merge them into one sorted list and print its values.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n1 and n2, the sizes of the two lists.
Second line: n1 integers (list 1, sorted).
Third line: n2 integers (list 2, sorted).
problems.outputFormat: The merged, sorted list values, space separated.
hints: Use two pointers, one for each list, and always take the smaller of the two current elements.
When one list is exhausted, append the rest of the other list directly.
This models the merge step of merge sort applied to linked lists.

problems.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
problems.statement: Given a linked list, remove the `n`-th node from the end of the list (1-indexed from the end) and print the resulting list.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: m (list size) and n.
Second line: m space-separated integers.
problems.outputFormat: The resulting list's values, space separated (empty line if the list becomes empty).
hints: Use a dummy node pointing to head so removing the actual head is not a special case.
Advance a 'fast' pointer n steps ahead of a 'slow' pointer, then move both until fast reaches the end.
Slow will now be right before the node to remove.

problems.title: Palindrome Linked List
problems.statement: Given a singly linked list, determine whether it is a palindrome (reads the same forward and backward).
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n.
Second line: n space-separated integers.
problems.outputFormat: Print "true" or "false".
hints: Find the middle of the list using slow/fast pointers.
Reverse the second half of the list in place.
Compare the first half and reversed second half node by node.

problems.title: Valid Parentheses
problems.statement: Given a string containing just the characters `(`, `)`, `{`, `}`, `[`, `]`, determine if the input string is valid. Brackets must close in the correct order.
problems.inputFormat: A single line containing the string.
problems.outputFormat: Print "true" or "false".
hints: Push opening brackets onto a stack.
On a closing bracket, check the top of the stack matches the corresponding opener, then pop.
The string is valid only if the stack is empty at the end.

problems.title: Min Stack
problems.statement: Design a stack that supports push, pop, top, and retrieving the minimum element, all in O(1) time. You'll process a sequence of operations from stdin.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: q (number of operations).
Each of the next q lines is one of:
`PUSH x`, `POP`, `TOP`, `GETMIN`.
problems.outputFormat: For each TOP or GETMIN operation, print the result on its own line.
constraints: Operations are always valid (no POP/TOP/GETMIN on an empty stack).

examples.input:
6
PUSH -2
PUSH 0
PUSH -3
GETMIN
POP
GETMIN

hints: Keep a second stack that tracks the minimum value at each point in time.
When pushing x, also push min(x, currentMin) onto the min-stack.
When popping, pop from both stacks together so they stay in sync.

problems.title: Next Greater Element
problems.statement: Given an array `nums`, for each element find the next element to its right that is strictly greater. If none exists, use -1.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n.
Second line: n space-separated integers.
problems.outputFormat: n space-separated integers: the next greater element for each position.
hints: Traverse from right to left (or left to right with a stack of pending indices).
Maintain a stack of indices whose next-greater element hasn't been found yet.
Pop from the stack while its top value is <= the current element, since the current element is their answer.

problems.title: Evaluate Postfix Expression
problems.statement: Evaluate an arithmetic expression given in postfix (Reverse Polish) notation. Tokens are space separated: integers and the operators `+ - * /`. Division truncates toward zero.
problems.inputFormat: A single line: the space-separated postfix expression.
problems.outputFormat: A single integer: the evaluated result.
hints: Split the line by spaces into tokens.
If a token is a number, push it. If it's an operator, pop two values (b then a), compute a OP b, and push the result.
The final answer is the single value left on the stack.

problems.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
problems.statement: Given an array of bar heights of a histogram (each bar has width 1), find the area of the largest rectangle that can be formed within the histogram.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n.
Second line: n space-separated non-negative integers.
problems.outputFormat: A single integer: the maximum rectangular area.
hints: For each bar, find how far it can extend left and right while remaining the shortest bar in that span.
A monotonic increasing stack of indices lets you compute this in a single pass.
When you pop an index because the current bar is shorter, the popped bar's rectangle width is (currentIndex - stack.top() - 1).

problems.title: Implement Queue using Stacks
problems.statement: Implement a FIFO queue using only stack operations, processing a stream of operations from stdin.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: q.
Each next line is `PUSH x` or `POP`.
problems.outputFormat: For each POP, print the removed value on its own line.
constraints: POP is never called on an empty queue.
hints: Keep two stacks: one for incoming pushes, one for outgoing pops.
On POP, if the 'out' stack is empty, dump everything from 'in' into 'out' (this reverses the order).
Then pop from 'out'. This gives amortized O(1) per operation.

problems.title: Design Circular Queue
problems.statement: Implement a fixed-capacity circular queue supporting enqueue, dequeue, and front, processing operations from stdin.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: capacity k and q (number of operations).
Each next line is `ENQUEUE x`, `DEQUEUE`, or `FRONT`.
problems.outputFormat: For ENQUEUE and DEQUEUE, print "true" if it succeeded or "false" if the queue was full/empty. For FRONT, print the front value or -1 if empty.
hints: Track `head` index and current `count` of elements; capacity is fixed at k.
Enqueue writes to index (head + count) % k, if count < k.
Dequeue advances head by 1 (mod k) and decrements count, if count > 0.

problems.title: First Negative Number in Every Window of Size K
problems.statement: Given an array and a window size `k`, find the first negative number in every contiguous window of size `k`. If a window has no negative number, print 0 for that window.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n and k.
Second line: n space-separated integers.
problems.outputFormat: (n - k + 1) space-separated integers, one per window.
hints: Maintain a deque of indices of negative numbers seen so far, in order.
Before reading each window's answer, pop indices from the front that have fallen out of the window.
The front of the deque (if any) is the first negative number in the current window.

problems.title: Sliding Window Maximum
problems.statement: Given an array `nums` and window size `k`, return the maximum value in every contiguous window of size `k`.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n and k.
Second line: n space-separated integers.
problems.outputFormat: (n - k + 1) space-separated integers: the max of each window.
hints: Maintain a deque of indices whose corresponding values are in decreasing order.
Before adding a new index, pop from the back while its value is <= the new value.
Pop from the front if it has fallen outside the current window; the front is always the current max.

problems.title: Generate Binary Numbers from 1 to N
problems.statement: Using a queue, generate the binary representations of all integers from 1 to `n`, in order.
problems.inputFormat: A single integer n.
problems.outputFormat: n lines, each the binary representation of 1, 2, ..., n in order.
hints: Start a queue with the string "1".
To get the next number, dequeue the front, print it, then enqueue front+"0" and front+"1".
Repeat this n times.

problems.title: Binary Search
problems.statement: Given a sorted array of distinct integers and a target value, return the index of the target, or -1 if it is not present.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n and target.
Second line: n space-separated sorted integers.
problems.outputFormat: A single integer: the index of target, or -1.
constraints: Array is sorted in strictly increasing order.
hints: Maintain lo = 0 and hi = n - 1, compute mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2.
If a[mid] == target, return mid. If a[mid] < target, search the right half, else the left half.
Stop when lo > hi and return -1.

problems.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
problems.statement: An array sorted in ascending order was rotated at an unknown pivot. Given the rotated array and a target, return its index, or -1 if absent. Must run in O(log n).
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n and target.
Second line: n space-separated integers (distinct values).
problems.outputFormat: A single integer: the index of target, or -1.
hints: At each step, one half of [lo, mid] or [mid, hi] is guaranteed to be normally sorted.
Check which half is sorted by comparing a[lo] and a[mid].
If the target lies within the sorted half's range, recurse there; otherwise recurse the other half.

problems.title: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
problems.statement: Given a sorted array and a target value, find the first and last index at which target appears. If it does not appear, return -1 -1.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n and target.
Second line: n space-separated sorted integers.
problems.outputFormat: Two space-separated integers: first index, last index (or -1 -1).
hints: Write a helper binary search that finds the leftmost index where a[i] >= target.
A similar search variant (leftmost index where a[i] > target, minus 1) gives the rightmost occurrence.
If the leftmost index found doesn't actually equal target, the answer is -1 -1.

problems.title: Find Peak Element
problems.statement: A peak element is one strictly greater than its neighbors (treat out-of-bounds neighbors as negative infinity). Given an array, find the index of any one peak. Must run in O(log n).
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n.
Second line: n space-separated integers (adjacent elements are never equal).
problems.outputFormat: A single integer: the index of a valid peak.
hints: Compare a[mid] with a[mid + 1]. If a[mid] < a[mid+1], a peak exists to the right.
Otherwise, a peak exists at mid or to its left.
This converges in O(log n) because you always move toward increasing values.

problems.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
problems.statement: Given two sorted arrays, find the median of the combined array. Must run in O(log(min(n, m))) time. Print the median with exactly 1 decimal place.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n and m.
Second line: n space-separated integers.
Third line: m space-separated integers.
problems.outputFormat: The median as a decimal number with exactly 1 decimal place.
hints: Binary search a partition point on the smaller array; the partition on the larger array is determined by it.
You want maxLeft <= minRight across both partitions combined.
If total length is even, median = (maxLeft + minRight) / 2.0; if odd, median = maxLeft of the larger partition side.

problems.title: Implement Bubble Sort
problems.statement: Given an array, sort it in ascending order using the bubble sort algorithm and print the result.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n.
Second line: n space-separated integers.
problems.outputFormat: n space-separated integers, sorted ascending.
hints: Repeatedly walk through the array, swapping adjacent elements that are out of order.
After each full pass, the largest unsorted element 'bubbles' to its correct position at the end.
You can stop early if a full pass makes no swaps.

problems.title: Implement Merge Sort
problems.statement: Given an array, sort it in ascending order using merge sort (O(n log n)) and print the result.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n.
Second line: n space-separated integers.
problems.outputFormat: n space-separated integers, sorted ascending.
hints: Base case: a subarray of length <= 1 is already sorted.
Recursively sort the left half [l, mid] and right half [mid+1, r].
Merge the two sorted halves using a temporary buffer, comparing front elements of each half.

problems.title: Implement Quick Sort
problems.statement: Given an array, sort it in ascending order using quick sort and print the result.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n.
Second line: n space-separated integers.
problems.outputFormat: n space-separated integers, sorted ascending.
hints: Choose a pivot (e.g. the last element) and partition so smaller elements end up left of it, larger to the right.
The Lomuto partition scheme uses a single index tracking the boundary of 'elements smaller than pivot'.
Recurse on the subarrays to the left and right of the pivot's final position.

problems.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
problems.statement: Given an array and an integer k, find the k-th largest element (1-indexed, so k=1 is the maximum).
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n and k.
Second line: n space-separated integers.
problems.outputFormat: A single integer: the k-th largest element.
hints: The simplest correct approach: sort descending and pick index k-1.
For better average performance, use quickselect (partition-based, like quicksort but recurse only one side).
A min-heap of size k is another O(n log k) approach: keep the k largest seen so far.

problems.title: Sort Colors (Dutch National Flag)
problems.statement: Given an array containing only 0s, 1s, and 2s, sort it in a single pass using O(1) extra space (the Dutch National Flag algorithm).
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n.
Second line: n space-separated integers, each 0, 1, or 2.
problems.outputFormat: n space-separated integers, sorted ascending.
hints: Maintain three pointers: low (boundary for 0s), mid (current), high (boundary for 2s).
If a[mid] == 0, swap with low and advance both low and mid.
If a[mid] == 2, swap with high and decrement high (don't advance mid yet, since the swapped-in value is unchecked).

problems.title: Binary Tree Inorder Traversal
problems.statement: Given a binary tree described in level-order (with -1 marking a null child), print its inorder traversal (left, root, right).
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n (number of values in the level-order description).
Second line: n space-separated integers, level-order, using -1 for null. The first value is always the root and is never -1.
problems.outputFormat: The inorder traversal, space separated. Print nothing (empty line) if the tree is empty.

examples.explanation: Root 1, left child 2 (leaf), right child 3 with children 4,5.

hints: Inorder means: recurse left, visit the node, recurse right.
A recursive helper function is the simplest approach.
You can also do it iteratively with an explicit stack if you want to avoid recursion.

problems.title: Height of Binary Tree
problems.statement: Given a binary tree in level-order (-1 for null), find its height (number of edges on the longest root-to-leaf path). A single node has height 0.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n.
Second line: n space-separated integers, level-order, -1 for null.
problems.outputFormat: A single integer: the height of the tree.
hints: height(node) = 1 + max(height(left), height(right)), with height(null) = -1.
A single-node tree should give height 0 by this formula.
This is a straightforward post-order recursion.

problems.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
problems.statement: Given a binary tree in level-order (-1 for null), print its level-order traversal, with each level on its own line.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n.
Second line: n space-separated integers, level-order, -1 for null.
problems.outputFormat: One line per level, containing that level's values space separated, top to bottom.
hints: Use a queue for BFS. Process the queue one full level at a time.
Before processing a level, record its current size (queue.size()) so you know how many nodes belong to it.
Push children as you pop each node in the current level.

problems.title: Lowest Common Ancestor in a BST
problems.statement: Given a binary search tree in level-order (-1 for null) and two values p and q known to exist in the tree, find the value of their lowest common ancestor.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n.
Second line: n space-separated integers, level-order, -1 for null (a valid BST).
Third line: p and q.
problems.outputFormat: A single integer: the value of the LCA.
constraints: p and q both exist in the tree and are distinct.
hints: In a BST, if both p and q are smaller than the current node, the LCA is in the left subtree.
If both are larger, the LCA is in the right subtree.
The first node where they diverge (or equal the node) is the LCA — you don't need recursion, a simple loop works.

problems.title: Diameter of Binary Tree
problems.statement: Given a binary tree in level-order (-1 for null), find its diameter: the length (in edges) of the longest path between any two nodes, which may or may not pass through the root.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n.
Second line: n space-separated integers, level-order, -1 for null.
problems.outputFormat: A single integer: the diameter.
hints: For each node, the longest path through it is leftDepth + rightDepth + 2 (in edges).
Compute depth recursively (post-order) and update a global 'best' diameter as you go.
The final answer is the max diameter found across all nodes, not just the root.

problems.title: Kth Smallest Element using a Heap
problems.statement: Given an array and integer k, find the k-th smallest element using a heap-based approach.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n and k.
Second line: n space-separated integers.
problems.outputFormat: A single integer: the k-th smallest element.
hints: Maintain a max-heap containing at most k elements — the k smallest seen so far.
For each new element, push it, and if the heap size exceeds k, pop the max.
After processing all elements, the top of the heap is the k-th smallest.

problems.title: Merge K Sorted Arrays
problems.statement: Given k sorted arrays, merge them into a single sorted array using a min-heap.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: k.
Each of the next k lines starts with the array's size followed by that many sorted integers.
problems.outputFormat: The fully merged, sorted array, space separated.
hints: Push the first element of each non-empty array into a min-heap, tagged with its array and index.
Pop the minimum, add it to the result, then push the next element from the same array (if any).
This runs in O(N log k) where N is the total number of elements.

problems.title: Top K Frequent Elements
problems.statement: Given an integer array and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements. If there is a tie in frequency, prefer the smaller value. Print them from most to least frequent.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n and k.
Second line: n space-separated integers.
problems.outputFormat: k space-separated integers: the top k frequent elements, most frequent first.
hints: First build a frequency map with an unordered_map.
Push (frequency, value) pairs into a max-heap, ordered by frequency desc then value asc.
Pop k elements from the heap to get the answer in the right order.

problems.title: Median in a Stream
problems.statement: Process a stream of integers one at a time. After each insertion, output the median of all numbers seen so far, using two heaps for O(log n) insertion.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n.
Second line: n space-separated integers, the stream in order.
problems.outputFormat: n lines: the median after each insertion. If the count is even, print the average of the two middle values (with 1 decimal place); if odd, print the middle value (also with 1 decimal place).
hints: Use a max-heap for the smaller half of numbers, and a min-heap for the larger half.
After every insertion, rebalance so the heap sizes differ by at most 1.
If sizes are equal, median = average of both tops; otherwise median = top of the larger heap.

problems.title: Connect Ropes with Minimum Cost
problems.statement: You have `n` ropes of given lengths. Connecting two ropes costs the sum of their lengths. Find the minimum total cost to connect all ropes into one.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n.
Second line: n space-separated positive integers, the rope lengths.
problems.outputFormat: A single integer: the minimum total cost.
hints: This is a classic greedy problem: always merge the two currently-smallest pieces.
Use a min-heap to always have quick access to the two smallest ropes.
Each merge cost adds to the total; push the merged length back into the heap.

problems.title: BFS Traversal of a Graph
problems.statement: Given an undirected graph with `n` nodes (0-indexed) and a list of edges, print the BFS traversal starting from node 0. When multiple neighbors are available, visit them in increasing order.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n and m (nodes, edges).
Each of the next m lines: u v, an edge between u and v.
problems.outputFormat: The BFS order, space separated.
hints: Use a queue and a visited array, standard BFS from node 0.
Sort each node's adjacency list so neighbors are visited in increasing order.
If the graph is disconnected, after finishing BFS from 0, continue BFS from any unvisited node in increasing order.

problems.title: DFS Traversal of a Graph
problems.statement: Given an undirected graph with `n` nodes and a list of edges, print the DFS traversal starting from node 0, visiting neighbors in increasing order.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n and m.
Each of the next m lines: u v.
problems.outputFormat: The DFS order, space separated.
hints: Standard recursive DFS: mark the node visited, record it, then recurse into each unvisited neighbor.
Sort adjacency lists first so neighbors are explored in increasing numeric order.
Handle disconnected graphs by starting a new DFS from any unvisited node after the first one finishes.

problems.title: Number of Islands
problems.statement: Given a grid of `1`s (land) and `0`s (water), count the number of islands. An island is formed by connecting adjacent lands horizontally or vertically.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: rows and cols.
Next `rows` lines: a string of `0`s and `1`s of length `cols`.
problems.outputFormat: A single integer: the number of islands.
hints: Scan every cell; when you find an unvisited '1', that's a new island — increment the count.
From that cell, flood-fill (BFS or DFS) marking all connected '1' cells as visited.
Only 4-directional adjacency (up/down/left/right) counts as connected.

problems.title: Detect Cycle in an Undirected Graph
problems.statement: Given an undirected graph, determine whether it contains a cycle.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n and m.
Each of the next m lines: u v.
problems.outputFormat: Print "true" if a cycle exists, otherwise "false".
hints: DFS approach: for each unvisited node, DFS while tracking the parent that led to the current node.
If you reach a visited neighbor that is NOT the parent, a cycle exists.
Alternatively, use union-find: if an edge connects two nodes already in the same set, that's a cycle.

problems.title: Dijkstra's Shortest Path
problems.statement: Given a weighted, undirected graph with `n` nodes and non-negative edge weights, find the shortest distance from node 0 to every other node. If a node is unreachable, its distance is -1.
problems.inputFormat:
First line: n and m.
Each of the next m lines: u v w (an edge between u and v with weight w).
problems.outputFormat: n space-separated integers: shortest distance from node 0 to node i, for i = 0..n-1.
hints: Use a min-heap (priority_queue) of (distance, node), always expanding the closest unvisited node.
Initialize all distances to infinity except node 0, which is 0.
When popping a node, if its recorded distance in the heap is stale (worse than the current best), skip it.

topicDescriptions.Arrays: Contiguous memory, prefix sums, two pointers, and the sliding window patterns that show up everywhere.
topicDescriptions.Linked List: Pointer manipulation, cycle detection, and in-place reversal without extra memory.
topicDescriptions.Stack: LIFO structures for parsing, monotonic sequences, and expression evaluation.
topicDescriptions.Queue: FIFO structures, circular buffers, and deque-based sliding window tricks.
topicDescriptions.Searching: Binary search and its many disguises, from rotated arrays to partition search.
topicDescriptions.Sorting: Classic sorting algorithms and the selection problems built on top of them.
topicDescriptions.Trees: Traversals, recursion, and structural properties of binary trees and BSTs.
topicDescriptions.Heap: Priority queues for top-k, streaming medians, and greedy merging problems.
topicDescriptions.Graphs: BFS, DFS, connectivity, and shortest paths on weighted and unweighted graphs.
